issues.legal_issue: A person who receives land by allotment after completion of a public-purpose acquisition has no right to participate in determining compensation for that acquisition.
material_facts: The land was acquired for a public purpose, vested in the State after the award and taking of possession, and was subsequently allotted to a company.
The allotment deed required the company to pay an additional price if compensation was enhanced.
The company sought to participate in the compensation proceedings, arguing that it would bear the financial consequences of enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The post-acquisition allottee had no locus to be heard and was neither a necessary nor a proper party to the compensation proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3(b) and 50 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the right to participate in compensation proceedings does not extend to a person who receives land from the State after a public-purpose acquisition has been completed. Once the land vests in the State, the State may transfer it on terms that do not give the former owner a concern in the transfer price or give the transferee a right to contest compensation. Order I Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not make a post-acquisition allottee a necessary or proper party merely because the acquiring authority may not effectively contest compensation or the allottee may be contractually liable for an increased price. The Court followed Hindu Kanya Maha Vidyalaya, Jind v. Municipal Committee, Jind and Peerappa Hanmantha Harijan v. State of Karnataka, and distinguished Himalayan Tiles and Marble (P) Ltd. v. Francis Victor Coutinho, Santosh Kumar v. Central Warehousing Corporation, Neyvely Lignite Corporation Ltd. v. Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition), U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad v. Gyan Devi, and Delhi Development Authority v. Bhola Nath Sharma because those cases concerned acquisitions for a company or statutory beneficiary, or otherwise did not establish a right for a post-acquisition allottee.

rule.if: public_purpose_acquisition and acquisition_completed_before_allotment and post_acquisition_allottee and allottee_seeks_to_participate_in_compensation

predicates.public_purpose_acquisition: The land was acquired by the State for a public purpose rather than acquired for the eventual allottee as the beneficiary.
predicates.acquisition_completed_before_allotment: The land had vested in the State after the award and taking of possession before it was transferred or allotted to the person seeking to participate.
predicates.post_acquisition_allottee: The person seeking to participate received the land from the State after completion of the acquisition.
predicates.allottee_seeks_to_participate_in_compens: The post-acquisition recipient sought to be heard in proceedings determining compensation for the acquired land.

issues.definition: When land is acquired for a public purpose, the acquisition is completed before the recipient receives the land, and that recipient seeks to participate in compensation proceedings, the recipient has no right to participate.

issues.legal_issue: Additional evidence may not be admitted in an appeal when none of the grounds for admitting it is established.
material_facts: In appeals concerning compensation, the acquiring authority and the allottee sought to adduce additional evidence.
The trial court had not refused to receive the evidence.
The evidence was not shown to have been unavailable despite due diligence.
The appellate court did not need the evidence to pronounce judgment.
issues.conclusion: The applications to adduce additional evidence should not have been allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Order XLI Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits additional evidence in an appeal only on specified grounds, including that the trial court refused evidence that ought to have been admitted, that despite due diligence the evidence was unavailable or could not be produced earlier, or that the appellate court requires it to pronounce judgment or for another substantial cause. Additional evidence cannot be used to fill a lacuna or patch up weak points in a case. The court must record reasons when allowing additional evidence.

rule.if: compensation_appeal_proceeding and additional_evidence_requested and trial_court_did_not_refuse_evidence and evidence_available_despite_due_diligence and appellate_court_does_not_need_evidence_to_decide

predicates.compensation_appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the determination of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.additional_evidence_requested: A party asked the appellate court to receive evidence that was not before the trial court.
predicates.trial_court_did_not_refuse_evidence: The trial court did not refuse to admit the evidence now offered on appeal.
predicates.evidence_available_despite_due_diligence: The evidence was available, or could have been produced, when the matter was before the trial court despite the party's exercise of due diligence.
predicates.appellate_court_does_not_need_evidence_t: The appellate court did not require the proposed evidence to pronounce judgment.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, if additional evidence is requested, the trial court did not refuse it, it was available despite due diligence, and the appellate court does not need it to decide, the evidence must not be admitted.

issues.legal_issue: A remand for fresh determination is unjustified when it rests on additional evidence that does not satisfy the requirements for admission.
material_facts: The appellate court allowed additional evidence and remanded the compensation matter for fresh decision.
The trial court had not refused the evidence, the evidence was not shown to have been unavailable despite due diligence, and it was not necessary for the appellate court to pronounce judgment.
The stated need for a fresh decision followed from the additional evidence and the opportunity to consider it.
issues.conclusion: There was no ground for remand, and the remand order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Order XLI Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure restricts the admission of additional evidence in an appeal to specified grounds. Where those grounds are not made out, additional evidence cannot justify reopening the matter, and the case should not be remanded on that basis.

predicates.compensation_appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the determination of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.remand_based_on_additional_evidence: The appellate court ordered a fresh determination because it allowed or proposed to consider additional evidence.
predicates.no_ground_for_admitting_additional_evide: The evidence was not refused by the trial court, was not shown to be unavailable despite due diligence, and was not needed by the appellate court to pronounce judgment or otherwise supported by a substantial cause.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal is remanded for a fresh determination based on additional evidence for which no ground for admission exists, the remand is unjustified.

issues.legal_issue: A prior order permitting a party to apply for impleadment or intervention does not itself establish a right to be impleaded or heard.
material_facts: In an earlier round, the Court stated that the allottee was free to apply for impleadment or for leave to act as an intervenor.
The allottee later relied on that statement to argue that its application had to be accepted.
The Court determined that the allottee had no right to participate in the compensation proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The earlier observation created no crystallized right; the application remained subject to determination according to law.
issues.legal_principle: Permission to file an application does not decide the merits of the application or create a right to the relief sought. The application must be considered according to law, including the governing rules on participation in compensation proceedings.

predicates.earlier_order_permits_application: An earlier court order stated that a person could apply to be added as a party or allowed to intervene.
predicates.application_later_made: The person later made the application contemplated by the earlier order.
predicates.applicant_has_no_substantive_participati: The person seeking to participate has no substantive right to be heard in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an earlier order permits an application, the application is later made, and the applicant lacks a substantive right to participate, the application must be determined under the applicable law rather than automatically granted.
